summary.headline: A week behind target: orders at 75.3% and revenue at 74.9%; the year sits at 83.7% of target, with the required pace far above the recent run-rate.

points.what: Orders came in at 678, 75.3% of the weekly target of 900.
points.so_what: The week added to the quarter's shortfall instead of closing any of it.

points.what: Revenue was $51,003, 74.9% of the weekly target, and both orders and revenue were down week on week.
points.so_what: The miss is broad rather than confined to one KPI, so no single measure carried the week.

points.what: Revenue grew 68.4% and orders 48.4% against the same week last year, both below the 75% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: Growth is real but slower than the targets were built on, so the gap to target keeps widening.

points.what: New customer signups fell 15.0% week on week to 233, a notably large drop, and were 3.7% below last year.
points.so_what: Signups are the only headline measure below last year while orders are well ahead, a divergence worth tracking.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is $29,480 below the target to date, with 10 weeks of the quarter left.
points.so_what: Three weeks in the quarter is already behind, and the gap grows with every further week near this level of attainment.

points.what: Signups dropped 15.0% week on week, a change the brief marks as notable, and are below last year.
points.so_what: This is the weakest of the customer-growth measures and is moving in the wrong direction on both comparisons.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 29 Dec 2025 was 11.2%, 1.0 pp above the same week last year.
points.so_what: Returns are running above last year's level, which works against gross revenue even in weeks when orders grow.

points.what: Orders finished 222 short of the weekly target and revenue $17,106 short.
points.so_what: The week did nothing to reduce the quarter-to-date shortfall and instead enlarged it.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue of $150,921 is 83.7% of the target to date for 2026-Q1.
points.so_what: Recovering the quarter would require later weeks to run above target, not merely reach it.

points.what: Reaching the full-year target of $3,888,802 requires $74,758 of revenue a week for the remaining 50 weeks, against a recent 8-week run-rate of $50,363.
points.so_what: The required pace is far above anything achieved recently, so at the current pace the full-year target is out of reach.

points.what: EMEA orders fell 15.4% to 115, a contribution of -21 orders and the largest single drag on the week.
points.so_what: One region accounted for more than the entire weekly decline, so the drop was concentrated rather than broad.

points.what: Search orders fell 4.0% to 481, contributing -20 orders.
points.so_what: The decline sits in the largest traffic source, so the smaller sources had no realistic scope to offset it.

points.what: APAC orders rose 4.7% to 309, adding 14 orders, and Email added 8.
points.so_what: Growth in the largest region and in Email is what kept the overall weekly decline to a small one.

points.what: AOV fell 4.0% to $84.86, still 5.4% above the same week last year.
points.so_what: Revenue fell further than orders this week, and the lower AOV is the difference between the two.

points.what: The cancellation rate improved 2.1 pp to 11.4%, a notable move, and is well below last year's 17.7%.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth $575 of revenue, so this improvement cushioned an otherwise weak revenue week.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 29 Dec 2025 eased 0.2 pp to 11.2%.
points.so_what: Week to week the measure is stable, so the issue is its level rather than its direction.

points.what: Orders of 678 sat just below the 8-week average of 683.
points.so_what: Weekly volume has been flat for two months while weekly targets step up, so the shortfall is not self-correcting.

summary.headline: Both orders and revenue finished the week behind target, at 75.3% and 74.9%; the quarter and the year now stand at 83.7% of target.

points.what: Orders came in at 678 against a target of 900, and revenue at $51,003 against $68,109.
points.so_what: Both headline KPIs missed, so the week added to the shortfall the quarter is carrying.

points.what: QTD and YTD revenue are both at 83.7% of target, $29,480 behind the target to date.
points.so_what: Three weeks into the year the gap to target is already material, with no surplus week to offset it.

points.what: Orders were down 1.5% week on week, while still 48.4% above the same week last year.
points.so_what: Year-on-year growth remains strong but sits below the 75% growth the targets assume, which is why attainment is under 100%.

points.what: The cancellation rate fell 2.1 pp to 11.4%, a notable move rated good.
points.so_what: Order quality improved even though the week itself finished behind target.

points.what: Revenue grew 68.4% year on year and orders 48.4%, against the 75% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: While growth stays below that rate, the gap to target widens week by week rather than closing.

points.what: New signups fell 15.0% week on week to 233, a notable move rated bad.
points.so_what: Customer additions moved down while orders held close to the recent level, a risk to watch in the coming weeks.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 29 Dec 2025 was 11.2%, up 1.0 pp year on year, rated bad.
points.so_what: Returns are running higher than a year ago, which weighs on the value of the revenue already booked.

points.what: Orders reached 75.3% of the weekly target and revenue 74.9%, a revenue gap of $17,106.
points.so_what: Both measures of the week fell short, so the week did nothing to recover the quarter's position.

points.what: QTD revenue of $150,921 is 83.7% of the target to date, leaving $623,634 of the $774,555 full-quarter target across 10 remaining weeks.
points.so_what: The quarter is behind after three weeks and the remaining weeks carry more than the original weekly pace assumed.

points.what: Hitting the $3,888,802 full-year target requires $74,758 of revenue a week for the remaining 50 weeks, against a recent 8-week run-rate of $50,363.
points.so_what: The required pace is far above what the business has been running, so the full-year target is out of reach at the current pace.

points.what: EMEA orders fell 15.4% to 115, a contribution of -21 orders and 210% of the week-on-week change.
points.so_what: EMEA was the single largest drag on the week's order decline; without it the total would have moved differently.

points.what: Search orders fell 4.0% to 481, contributing -20 orders and 200% of the change, on a 70.9% share of orders.
points.so_what: With Search holding the bulk of volume, its direction sets the direction of total orders.

points.what: APAC orders rose 4.7% to 309, contributing 14 orders.
points.so_what: The APAC gain was not enough to offset the declines elsewhere, so total orders still fell.

points.what: AOV fell 4.0% to $84.86, though it remains 5.4% above the same week last year.
points.so_what: Revenue fell faster than orders this week, so smaller baskets added to the order decline rather than cushioning it.

points.what: The cancellation rate of 11.4% is down from 17.7% a year ago, with each percentage point worth about $575 of revenue.
points.so_what: Fewer cancellations protected revenue this week and partly limited the size of the miss against target.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 29 Dec 2025 eased 0.2 pp to 11.2%.
points.so_what: Week to week returns are broadly flat, so the year-on-year rise is the part of this measure that matters.

points.what: Orders of 678 sat just below the 8-week average of 683.
points.so_what: The week tracked the recent run-rate rather than stepping up towards the weekly target level.
